content.text: Everything else about "what should I work on now" is answerable — hierarchy through epic_key/parent_key, releases through fix_versions. Sprint is not answerable at all.
gadak: cannot apply JQL — sprint in (openSprints()) (not in the subset)   [exit 1]
$ gadak --workspace demo search --jql 'project = NMA AND sprint = 12' --json
warning: JQL skipped sprint = 12 (not in the subset)

There is no sprint column (pragma table_info(issues)) and internal/sync/sync.go:43-48 baseFields does not fetch the sprint custom field on incremental sync. The oss mirror already carries a saved filter named "gadak-test: sprint leftover" whose recorded unsupported clause is exactly this. The JQL subset decision (docs/decisions/0007) refuses the openSprints() function.

Fix shape: project sprint id, name and state (future/active/closed) onto the issue — not a board table. Discover the field id through the existing `gadak fields` machinery; never hardcode a customfield id, since it differs per site. Extend the JQL subset with sprint = <id> and sprint in openSprints() (state = active) and say so in the documented subset. Key SQL on the id, never on "Sprint 41". A site with no sprint field yields empty, not an error. issuetap gets a fixture custom field at most — no Agile API, no boards (boards are explicitly out of scope in spec.md and remain a 501 there).
Gate: FAIL-first is the exit 1 above; afterwards sprint appears in applied and not in unsupported, and the SQL by sprint id returns the same key set as the JQL.
Not Highest because neither dogfood site (oss, default) fills sprints — this is for Scrum-shaped Jira, where nothing substitutes for it.
Found by the Jira-surface gap sweep (track A, score 9/10).
